text: Bourbon Street and all of it's fame is a half block away, but this deserves to be one of the most famous spots in the French Quarter. Before we get to anything else - they are serious about that dress code and they seem to always be packed. Do yourself a favor and plan ahead if you want to visit. The menu changes often, so it's possible to miss out on the dish you wanted if you have to come back the next day. There are some inventive dishes here - the Tempura Fin wings somehow get all of the great parts of chicken wings but are made from fish. They used to call canned tuna the "chicken of the sea" but this is something different and delicious - they turn the fin section of the catch of the day into a great snack - they take the part that you normally throw away and make it great. I know it's a seafood restaurant, but the pork chop is worth it - the sides and preparation changes often, but it is excellent. The star of the menu is the scalibut - part scallop, part halibut and all good. The scallops are thinly sliced and use as a crust for the halibut, sealing in the flavors and providing a different texture than you would expect. It may sound strange, but it's great. This is an expensive dinner - there were people there celebrating birthdays and other special occasions, so I would suggest making one up to give yourself an excuse to go there and eat. A solid five star place.

text: If I could distill the coolness of Baltimore Ave in the 90s, before Penn's community exploded, I'd say the barn is a pretty good representation of what grade school me would have thought a bar in West Philly would be like. I'm pretty sure Patrick Swayze's inexplicable presence (RIP) would be the only thing that would make things cooler. Here is what you need to do to enjoy the barn: 1. Get a drink. 2. Enjoy the music or watch some TV. 3. Oh hey, they have food. That's not what you're here for so if you're judging it one way or the other you're ignoring steps 1 and 2. The most 90s Philly thing about the Barn is that it's not a destination. It's the anti-destination. You just end up there because of a school trip or something and find out, hey, this place rules. Don't come here for handmade cocktails - come here for a strong pour of x liquor plus y mixer. Don't come here for beers you can only get in 5 places on the East Coast - they have everything local (and macro) that you might need. Don't come here for haute cuisine - come here for bigass piles of greasy goodness that will armor your stomach for too many shots. And while I'm on the subject of "handmade cocktails," I don't even know how to process that idea. For the record, I love cocktails. But how the hell were we making cocktails before? With robots? Why did we stop? Because of what happened in Terminator 2? Ah, 90s Philly.

text: I write this poor review as a food service professional, though not as a competitor. I'm deeply concerned about how little most establishments contribute to their communities because they don't understand or practice basic synergistic principles. I get that Cat Cora started this chain, and that she was on Iron Chef--but how does that translate into quality and value? The short answer is it doesn't. Gimmick food isn't in itself valuable. Extracting value from employees or customers by producing as little as possible for as much as possible doesn't create value for anyone. That approach is a dead end street. Today's foray into the Goleta shop didn't result in a purchase--for reasons I will lay out shortly. However, I have eaten a Mesa Burger at the Mesa location--it was so-so. I can get an equivalent burger or better at the original Habit in Goleta (yup, smaller patty, but better overall flavor, price and experience). No, today's experience resulted in us walking out before we had even made a purchase. And let me tell you why... Any kind of food service (really, any sort of service) business is far more than a production line of food. It is far more than whether that food is quality or not. It is far more than how much profit the operator can achieve. In its potential form, it is an access point to quality in various forms that goes from the operator to the community and back. Here was our experience today: We walked up to the counter with only one small group of about three adults in front of us ordering. There was one young male taking their order and two young females standing by doing nothing, while looking generally in the our direction--new customers. We stood there for some time with the two females alternately talking to each other and staring off into space. One of those females wandered over to the service counter, where she touched her own hair, jean jacket and ear and then laid her head on her arms on the service counter, with her hair on the counter. She then moved back to the main counter (again, facing us) when the other female moved to take a bottle of apple juice out of the cooler and place it on the counter. She then opened the bottle of juice, poured it into a plastic cup and with the same hands she had touched herself with without gloves she grabbed a lid for the cup and affixed it to the cup. None of the three counter employees acknowledged my wife or me during this whole time. Still waiting, my wife and I then conferred with each other standing just behind and to the side of the people ordering--in plain sight of all three employees--and eventually decided we wouldn't participate in this kind of customer service nightmare and walked out (there was no one behind us and maybe 10 customers total in the restaurant; there were clearly at least three cooks in the kitchen; it wasn't in any sense a stressed environment). So, reader, whom are we taking to task? It's not the employees. Their behavior was far from exemplary, but this is about management. (Hint: it's always about management.) If your idea is about making some gimmicky food and then turning it over to a general manager or shift manager and you think you are going to make money or even (as much as I think this isn't in your head or heart at all) be a part of the community and care about the value you create--you are completely blind. This isn't creativity or artistry or even good food. It's crap. You don't do your employees or customers or community any good. Why should any of us shovel money at you for this?

start, will have to wait and see how productive that one plant's going to be. the eggplants were extra VERY disappointing. in three plantings, two varieties, got just zero plants. i've noticed there's an inverse relationship between how much marketing a company does and the quality of their products. good companies count on repeat business and word-of-mouth for sales. bad companies count on text: This is a small regional airport (also moonlights an international airport too, apparently) that services some regional airlines not serviced by the much bigger sister airport in Tampa. Facilities here are good w/clean restrooms and a quick n easy TSA checkpoint. There are a lot of seating option in the gate areas; some are even comfy chairs w/charging platforms attached. The boarding here is a little off-kilter, however, as several flights seem to arrive at the same time and it gets a bit chaotic. So, pro-tip: just wait for everyone to do their thing even if your boarding section is called. You are all going to the same place. I did this my second time around and it was a much less stressful process. Also, they do not have jetways here; you board and de-plane on the tarmac. There is a lot of construction around the entrance and exit to the airport, so do not follow your GPS. I had a couple of ride-share mishaps that took us to this very scary looking abandoned field instead of the airport, just follow the signage off the highway and navigate the labyrinth of cones. Drop-off here is much easier than pick-up. It is literally the same stretch of road, just at opposite ends of the airport. It is honestly easier to get picked up at the drop-off entrance as the designated pick-up section is small and it gets congested due to the bottle-neck of cars trying to pull out while others are pulling in. I think once the construction mess is done, this airport will reach its full potential, until then 2-stars because they definitely could have better signage navigating to the airport as well as exiting. It is absolutely fine once you are inside, but getting there is another story. I have heard a bunch of people complain about what a mess the parking situation is, so take that into consideration if you are flying out and plan to leave your car.

text: TL;DNR version: LiceDoctors didn't show up on two different appointments and caused us more stress than we needed to deal with. Full Review: We found out on Sunday that our daughter had nits. We called and the LiceDoctors were able to schedule a same-day appointment in our house. An hour later, we get a call from them saying the technician was having car trouble and couldn't make it that day. We rescheduled for 12:30 pm the next day and called the morning of the appointment to confirm. When 12:30 came and went, we called and was told "Well, we actually give our technicians a window, yours should be there by 1:30". As you may guess, the technician didn't show up. The customer service rep asked us to give her more time and we did. By 2:00, we asked the rep to please call the technician and call us back. The rep did not call us back, so we called back 20 minutes later to find out our scheduled technician wasn't responding to calls or texts. They said they would look for other technicians who could come our way and we never heard from them. As it was becoming more apparent that an in-home appointment wasn't going to happen, we were able to find another business we could take our daughter to. When I told them about the scheduling snafu, they said "Let me guess, LiceDoctors? We hear about this all the time". Also, after more research on their treatment methods, we discovered that we were going to need to continue daily treatments of her hair for three weeks. At the price we were prepared to pay for the treatment, that seems absurd. We ended up using Lice Slayers, whose price was comparable, offers a one-treatment guarantee, a free re-check after two weeks, and a free treatment if any remaining nits/lice are found. If you're dealing with the stress of trying to figure out what to do about nits/lice in your home, don't rely on the LiceDoctors.

text: My wife and I came here a few weeks ago for our anniversary and they did not disappoint. I made a reservation with OpenTable and made a notation that we were celebrating our anniversary. The restaurant was clean, but had that old school, mafia vibe. Like a scene from Godfather--dark, photos on the wall, tiled floor, dark wood. It did not have the hip ambiance of Desi Vega's. No, this was the place for folks like Archie Manning, who was seated near the front windows of the restaurant. It reminded me of an old Dickey Brennan's, like in need of a reno. Well, the food was delicious. I wasn't crazy about my seafood soup that only had one oyster and one shrimp in it and I wasn't crazy about our $31 lobster tail. That was so overpriced and didn't have much flavor. The highlight dishes were everything else--who dat shrimp (wrapped in bacon and dressed with this delectable sauce); we get this dish whenever we visit Desi's; crab cake, and, yes, it was sizzling and mostly crab; ribeye, so tender, moist, and flavorful, despite being well done; and a side of lyonnaise potatoes. I've heard these called brabant potatoes in other restaurants. Crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside. They surprised us with a complimentary ooey-gooey bread pudding dessert at the end. It was small, but we were watching our carb intake. Not sure how to describe the dessert, but it was a tasty treat. We can check this box as we make our steakhouse rounds.

text: An honest review from a minor who has been admitted twice: When I was thirteen I was admitted to West Hills after a failed suicide attempt. My parents and I were left to the streets after being told there wasn't enough beds for me to stay. Later that night they called and informed my mother that they did in fact have an opening. When I got there I found an entirely empty hall which has lead us to believe that they did in fact have rooms open, but pushed away a scared family who needed help. Once I was there the treatment was terrible. They claim that you see a therapist every day and your doctor at least once a day too. I saw Doctor Thomas a total of three times in a my week long stay and never once met a therapist. We had "group therapy" all day where all the patients just sat in a room together and prayed that they'd just release us. A lot of the staff were also not qualified to be "helping" young children with mental illnesses. One mental health technician told us that he was in fact high off of weed during his shift with us. Another informed us that she was cheating on her long time boyfriend with three other men. If anyone can tell me that that is professional, I'd love to hear your argument. I also told my doctor that the medicine I was on had terrible side effects and I was not okay with taking it. Her response was simply upping my dosage. After feeling like my opinion on my health was useless, I quickly stopped taking my medicine cold turkey after being released. This lead to my last suicide attempt two years later when I was then again admitted into West Hills. It's sense been a year from my last visit and I still have nightmares about the place. I met with my doctor once in my five day long stay. At the time I didn't even know he was my doctor. Then upon discharge he informed me that once I'm released he will send a prescription for an antidepressant to my pharmacy. After being discharged for three weeks and leaving countless voicemails to my doctor he finally sent the prescription over. If I could give this institution a negative review I would. Words cannot explain the trauma this place has put on me. If you are considering admitting your child here, please don't for the sake of them. Instead take them to your local Boys and Girls Club. It's a lot cheaper and will treat your children even better than West Hills. BGC may even help more.

Was I requesting a beer with a free ticket I received for being there? Yes. Would that beer be the last drink I ordered in the evening? Not at all, I preferred drinks off the menu and wanted to try other things on tap or a cocktail from their fresh ingredients; but first beer was the last and I didn't even finish it because I was disappointed with my experience. After I received the reply I got, I stated that my wife and I were waiting there for 20 minutes and he argued that I was not, granted it was probably more like 15 minutes, but in all reality, that is unreasonable. I was still a bit confused since I've always tried other brands from other eye doctors in previous states without an issue. (Virginia, Georgia, and North Carolina). Those eye care professionals only required I stay with the same power and always approved the prescription for Lens.com or 1-800 Contacts. When I received the call back from Eagle Eye, I was informed that I would need to come in for a contact fitting at no charge. We discussed possible days I was available to come in, and the receptionist put me on hold to check the schedule. Upon returning to the call 12 minutes later; she said I was last seen in March, "so since it had almost been a year" (it's only been 8 months) I could just schedule my annual visit and that "my eyesight may have changed which could be part of my problem with the other contact lenses." She then said if I still just wanted to come in for the fitting, it would be $60. When I stated that she told me there would be no charge for the fitting, she said she didn't realize how long it had been. She informed me the office policy was that I had 60 days after my appointment to let the doctor know if the contacts did not work in order to have a fitting for a different brand without charge. Then she said, "it's really 90 days because we grant a 30-day grace period to change without charge past the 60 days." I told her that I thought it was poor customer service to tell someone they would not be charged then put them on hold to make the appointment only to return and tell them to either pay for an annual visit or pay $60 for a fitting. I also told her I did not understand why a different brand of lenses was approved by the office TWICE before if I was supposed to come in for another fitting. She told me that I'd likely submitted the prescription near the weekend and Lens.com can fill a prescription if they don't hear back from the doctor's office for 48 hours. She then told me she'd lived in Florida her entire life and it was Florida LAW to order the same brand of lens that appears on the prescription. This seems like a way to get more money from the customer. It is a shame that my business as a new customer and referrals were not worth more to this practice. text: I love being surprised by a restaurant. I had never heard of this place, didn't really look at too many pictures, and showed up. The wine glasses are plastic and the tables/chairs aren't fancy by any means. For food you get a great 25$ price fixed menu. Got the escargot and absolutely loved it. Not overpowering on the peppercorn and snail cooked well, didn't come out tough. For dinner got the duck leg - while I was hoping the portion was slightly bigger, it was delicious. The sauce paired really well with the meat and halfway through our meal, Chef Marc came over and talked with us about the place and the food. He's a great guy and apparently this is also a night spot as well. Interested to go back a second time and try some other dishes. This place is a well kept secret that I know will start to become more than that soon.

text: We live in Southampton and have been to Russells without exaggeration dozens of times. The food is good, and the atmosphere is nice and it was a lovely addition to the neighborhood. However, I feel compelled to write a review after a number of experiences we have had with the staff recently. We often joked that the service was slow but it was okay because it gave us lots of time to drink our coffee. What is not okay is eye rolling and rudeness...both if which we have experienced the last several times we have been there. Last month we were there with my parents and our server seemed bothered to have to wait on us in the first place, and irritated when my mom asked for a box. She has been there forever, this is not uncommon for her. Many times we have watched her walk away from other tables rolling her eyes and complaining about her customers to other staff...it's a small place it's hard to miss that behavior. She's done it with us before as well. Annoying, but we overlooked it because we enjoyed the restaurant. Today we went in and when they offered us a table on the enclosed deck, we said we would rather wait for a table inside. This flustered the hostess, and as we passed the other hostess she explained what we requested and the other hostess rolled her eyes as she passed us. As we waited outside in the cold for our table we realized how totally ridiculous this is. We are happy to overlook quirks and slow service to patronize a neighborhood spot, but patronizing a business where the employees are repeatedly rude just doesnt make sense. Farewell, Russells. We had a good run.
label: NEG
